baseline_audit.informal: For fixed tensor order $d\ge2$, accuracy and confidence, the worst-case embedding cost of independent isotropic sub-Gaussian tensor-product probes has rank order $r\log^{d-1}(er)$ for factor classes containing the independent-sign witnesses. The upper guarantee is uniform over fixed subspaces and admissible mode dimensions. Explicit independent-sign constructions give the matching obstruction.
hypotheses: $d\ge2$, mode dimensions $n_1,\ldots,n_d$, $r\ge1$ and a deterministic isometry $U:\mathbb R^r\to\bigotimes_j\mathbb R^{n_j}$
The $m$ probe rows are iid tensor products $z_i=\bigotimes_jg_i^{(j)}$; factors are independent and isotropic, with arbitrary coordinate dependence within each factor
$K>0$ and $\mathbb E\exp(\langle u,g^{(j)}\rangle^2/K^2)\le2$ for every unit $u$ and every factor
baseline_audit.conclusion: There is a constant $C_{d,K}>0$ such that $m\ge C_{d,K}[rt/\varepsilon^2+(rt^{d-1}+t^d)/\varepsilon]$ implies $\mathbb P\{\Pi\text{ fails to embed }\operatorname{range}(U)\text{ with squared-norm distortion }\varepsilon\}\le\delta$. Conversely, put $k=d-1$, $h=\lfloor\log r/(2k\log2)\rfloor$ and $c_d=[2(4k\log2)^k]^{-1}$. For $r\ge2^{4k}$ the explicit independent-sign construction with mode dimensions $(r,h,\ldots,h)$ has failure probability at least $1-\exp(-\sqrt r)$ for every integer $1\le m\le c_dr(\log r)^k$ and every $\varepsilon<1$. Thus the fixed-parameter rank order is sharp; the lower claim concerns these constructed subspaces, not every subspace or every factor law.

records.readback: The upper theorem quantifies actual independent probability laws on each vector factor, assumes coordinate second moments equal to the identity and the lower Lebesgue exponential-square integral bound on every unit direction, and concludes the actual iid normalized tensor sketch fails IsSubspaceEmbedding with probability at most delta. It takes no moment, one-step recursion, covariance tail or missing-proof hypothesis. The frame is deterministic and orthonormal. Its constant depends only on order and K; max(1,K) enlarges only internal coefficients. The full sample budget has variance r*t/epsilon^2 and large-row (r*t^(d-1)+t^d)/epsilon, t=log(4r/delta). A separate proved arithmetic and probability corollary yields r(1+log r)^(d-1) growth at fixed parameters. The Rademacher specialization discharges all factor hypotheses at K=10, a sufficient unoptimized parameter. The lower construction has first mode r and common modes h=floor(log r/(2(d-1)log 2)); its explicit frame has orthonormal columns and does not depend on sample width. Coordinate bijectivity, the literal probe identity and measure-preserving factor regrouping identify it with the same independent tensor construction. For r>=2^(4(d-1)), every positive width up to r(log r)^(d-1)/[2(4(d-1)log 2)^(d-1)] has failure at least 1-exp(-sqrt r), at every distortion below one. The rank-deficient width branch is included. Sharpness applies to classes containing this sign witness, not every law or every K>0. The source Gaussian/spherical lower variants and approximation results are not claims of this card.
